units.title: HyperEVM
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Known weaknesses. Collect security advisories, audit reports, bug bounty write-ups, incident post-mortems and open issues for this network's execution client, precompiles and system contracts from the last two years, including behaviour the network calls by design. For each, decide whether an ordinary account could use it against funds in the PoolManager.

code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 13 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software; Python 3, rustc 1.97 and node are present. Leads L-700, L-676, L-692 and L-693. On Monad a simulated call always runs the interpreter (monad_executor.cpp lines 1306-1309 at v0.16.7), so no opcode vector has ever run on the native code that block execution may use. Get producer evidence for the arithmetic the PoolManager depends on. Step 1: say whether any Monad RPC method executes on the block execution VM instead of the InterpreterOnly VM (eth_simulateV1, debug_traceTransaction, debug_traceBlockByNumber, debug_traceCall, a replay endpoint), from the source at the release the endpoints report, and if one exists run research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/battery.py and pmdiff6.py inputs through it. Step 2, independent of step 1: mined evidence from other contracts. Uniswap v3 style pools on Monad run the same FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, TickMath and SwapMath code shapes and have deep liquidity. Collect mined Swap events of the largest v3 style pools on Monad (and of the v4 PoolManager), select the swaps whose single step needs a 512 bit product (liquidity times the change of sqrtPriceX96 at or above 2^160, or amount times sqrtPriceX96 at or above 2^256, the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp), and check each against the exact formulas in v4math.py or a v3 transcription of them, using slot0 and liquidity read at the parent block. Report how many swaps exercise each large-number branch and whether every one matches to the unit. Plant a fault (a MULMOD result off by one for modulus 2^256-1) and show the check catches it. Step 3: say from the Monad source whether a contract of the v3 pool's size and of the PoolManager's size (24,009 bytes) is compiled, by reading the size estimate code path (vm.cpp, x86.hpp, emitter) and, if the bound cannot be computed without a build, by any observable that differs between compiled and interpreted execution in mined data (for example gas used on an out-of-gas halt, or the generic failure the RPC comment mentions). Step 4 (L-693): do the Monad PositionManager or the routers ever call clear(), transferFrom, burn through an operator, approve or donate on the PoolManager? Search mined transactions by selector in call traces over the full history if an endpoint allows it. For every claim give the endpoint, block numbers and counts. Record anything that does not match as a finding with the transaction hash.

Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software; Python 3, rustc 1.97 and node are present. Leads L-701, L-692, L-714 and L-618. MegaETH's sequencer executor is closed and compiles; HyperEVM's validator (hl-node) is closed. Cycle 13 replayed 1,566 MegaETH and 2,762 HyperEVM mined PoolManager transactions (research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-mined-branches.work/pmreplay.py and report.json) and all match, but these PoolManager branches have no mined instance on either network: the 512 bit branch of FullMath.mulDiv, the overflow fallback of SqrtPriceMath.getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp, clear of an exact credit, transferFrom with an allowance, burns through an operator, approve, donate, and swaps that end exactly on an initialized tick. Get producer evidence for the same operand classes from other mined transactions. (1) Widen the PoolManager window to the full history of each network and look again for each missing branch (use the jump map research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json and the selectors). (2) For the arithmetic branches, use Uniswap v3 style pools and other contracts that share FullMath: select mined swaps whose step needs a 512 bit product (liquidity times the change of sqrtPriceX96 at or above 2^160) or the overflow fallback, and check the event amounts against the exact formulas from parent-block state. (3) For MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 and a nonzero high word, and full-width DIV, any mined transaction whose trace or result depends on them will do; compare the sequencer's logs and storage with a re-execution in the reference interpreter. (4) L-714: for the 104 HyperEVM multi-step swaps whose tick spacing cycle 13 found by search, read the Initialize events over the PoolManager's full history and replay again with the real key (research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-swap-residuals.work/replay2.py). (5) L-618: anything public that names hl-node's EVM, its revm and ruint versions. Plant a fault in the reference to show each check can fail. Report counts per network and per branch, and record any mismatch as a finding with the transaction hash.

Do not install software; Python 3, rustc 1.97 and node are present. Leads L-702 and L-703. reth v2.2.0 had an execution cache fault: for an account without code that a block deleted and created again, the cache dropped the account entry and kept its cached storage words, so a later block read stale storage (crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs lines 857-882 at v2.2.0; fixed by reth pull request 28148; Arc fixed it in v0.8.5; recorded as F-124). For every reth based client among the 21 networks at the revision its endpoint reports today (query web3_clientVersion first and record it): Ethereum reth v2.11.0, OP Mainnet op-reth, Unichain, Ink and Soneium op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 (commit 65e80332), Base v1.5.6, Zora conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, World Chain, Celo reth v2.2.0-74cc8bb, X Layer reth v2.3.0-f60420a, MegaETH mega-reth v2.2.3 (what is public), Tempo v1.19.1, Arc v0.8.6 and reth-bsc: (a) is the old branch present at the pinned reth revision; (b) is the cache used by the sequencer's payload builder or block producer, or only by engine-tree validation on follower nodes; (c) which reads of the PoolManager could go stale: its own storage and transient storage, the balanceOf staticcall of sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), token code and storage, hook code. State exactly which accounts can reach the stale branch, including accounts with an EIP-7702 delegation designator and accounts emptied under EIP-161, and whether any contract a victim pool depends on (token, hook, router, PositionManager, Permit2) can be such an account. (d) On an L2 where the sequencer would serve stale storage and the proof program would not, say what an ordinary account could gain or block. Second part (L-703): read what changed in op-reth between v2.10.0-rc.1 and v2.10.0-rc.4 in the engine tree, execution cache, prewarming, state root task and the op-revm handler, and say whether any change can alter a storage, transient storage, balance or code read inside a transaction. Also read the other caches in front of state on these clients (precompile cache, bytecode cache, sparse trie cache) for a key that is not the full content or address. Record a network where the old branch is present on the producing path as a finding with the file and line.

Do not install software; Python 3, rustc 1.97 and node are present. Leads L-709, L-704, L-694 and L-695. Cycle 13's work is in research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-proof-builds-2.work (kona/scan_prestate.py, kona/mips64emu.py, kona/run_vectors.py, base/rv64emu.py, base/run_vectors.py, base/proof-contracts.md, celo/). The downloaded images and builds were not kept; fetch them again as needed into your own work directory. (1) L-709: LLVM issue 235261 miscompiles 128 bit shifts by 64 to 127 on MIPS64 under some constant folds, and kona-client 1.9.0 (respected prestate 0x03e5a548...37c9 for OP Mainnet, Unichain and Ink) was built with a toolchain that predates the fix. The cycle 13 scan followed straight-line code for at most 47 instructions from each of the 66 andi rX,rY,0x40 sites. Extend it to a control flow graph: follow branch and jump targets and delay slots from each site until rX is redefined on every path, and report whether any path reads the 0-or-64 value in xori, ori, addu, daddu, sltu, a multiply or a store. Confirm first, by eth_call on Ethereum, which prestate each of the three chains respects today. (2) L-695: if feasible in the emulator, run the real kona-client ELF routines for U256 shl, shr and sar (locate them by symbol or by pattern) on the shift vectors of research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/targeted.py, instead of a rebuild. (3) L-704: read by eth_call on Ethereum the wasmModuleRoot of the Arbitrum One rollup and of the Robinhood Chain rollup (and Elysium's parent chain if it has one), find the public consensus release that publishes that module root, and name the go-ethereum commit its replay binary pins. Compare that commit's core/vm arithmetic, jump destination analysis and transient storage files with go-ethereum 0e44603, which cycles 9 to 12 read. (4) L-694: for Base (game type 621, range program at base/base 6efa7566), Celo (type 42) and X Layer (type 1961), identify the published range program ELF or its verification key source, and say whether the toolchain it was built with (succinct rust toolchain version) carries any LLVM RISC-V fault that touches 128 bit multiply, shift or division lowering. If an ELF can be downloaded, run the U256 handlers in it on the targeted vectors with the RV64IM emulator. Report each as cleared, finding or inconclusive with the evidence. A divergence between a permissionless proof program and the node on any opcode the PoolManager runs is a finding an ordinary account could use.
